pcr-cycle.alt: Three panels of one PCR cycle. Denaturation at about 95 degrees Celsius: heat separates the two strands of the target region. Annealing at about 55 degrees: a primer pairs with each strand at opposite ends of the target, pointing inward. Extension at about 72 degrees: Taq polymerase extends each primer from its 3-prime end, building new DNA 5-prime to 3-prime. Below, copies double each cycle: 1, 2, 4, 8; after n cycles there are 2 to the n copies, about a billion after 30 cycles.

gel-electrophoresis.alt: An agarose gel with wells at the top near the negative electrode and the positive electrode at the bottom. Lane 1 is a DNA ladder with bands at 10,000, 5,000, 3,000, 2,000, 1,000 and 500 base pairs, the small fragments lowest. Three sample lanes show bands at 4,500 and 1,500; at 3,500, 1,500 and 1,000; and at 6,000 base pairs. Notes: DNA is negative, so it moves toward the positive electrode, and small fragments slip through the gel fastest and travel farthest.
